rules.when: At least one concrete violation of an applicable frozen requirement is established
rules.privacySecurityPolicy: Any demonstrated privacy or security violation requires rejection; other passing behavior cannot compensate.

rules.when: No violation is demonstrated and material gaps leave compliance unestablished
rules.note: Weak or vacuous tests establish a test-quality problem, not automatically a code defect.

rules.when: Applicable requirements are supported by sufficient inspectable evidence and no unresolved material violation or gap remains
rules.note: This is acceptance under the declared experimental scope, not production deployment approval.

constraints: Security concerns must cite an applicable requirement and evidence; unsupported suspicion cannot be scored as an established violation.
Unresolved privacy or security concerns trigger request-more-evidence and prevent acceptance until resolved.
Nested debug fields are user-visible response data and cannot disclose forbidden personal values.
A valid alternative implementation is not a defect merely because its internal code differs.
Different requirements adopted later do not retroactively change earlier study labels.
Code compliance and the quality of supplied tests are scored separately; independent source or execution evidence may support compliance despite a weak individual test.
metrics: false acceptance and false rejection against adjudicated implementation labels
uncertain and request-more-evidence counts reported separately
scopeNote: No production release gate, statistical performance claim, or independent label certification is established by this rubric.
